body:
## Summary

After fixing installed payload modes, `noemaforge smoke` started executing correctly, but it failed in `runtime_only` because the main backend socket was intentionally absent.

This is a post-install validation semantics issue. `runtime_only` explicitly starts gateway + ToolProxy only and skips the main LLM backend. Therefore a missing `/run/noemaforge/llm/backends/main.sock` should be treated as an expected skip/degraded state for that profile, not as an install/runtime failure.

## Environment

- NoemaForge CLI: `0.33.0`
- Branch: `release/0.33.0-dev`
- Start mode: `sudo noemaforge safe-start --wait --llm-profile=runtime_only`
- Observed services: gateway + ToolProxy active, no main backend

## Evidence

`safe-start runtime_only` logs say the main backend is intentionally skipped:

```text
[noemaforge-safe-start] runtime_only profile: enforcing no active main backend.
[noemaforge-safe-start] stopping stale main backend if present...
[noemaforge-safe-start] runtime_only profile: skipping modelstore/backend start.
[noemaforge-safe-start] runtime_only profile: gateway/toolproxy started; main backend not started.
```

But `noemaforge smoke` reports:

```text
[noemaforge-smoke][WARN] backend socket missing: /run/noemaforge/llm/backends/main.sock
=== NoemaForge smoke ===
backend socket: /run/noemaforge/llm/backends/main.sock
backend health: fail
backend chat:   fail response=<empty>
gateway socket: /run/noemaforge/llm/gateway.sock
gateway health: ok
gateway chat:   non_ok_response response=<empty>
overall:        fail

=== NoemaForge smoke debug ===
backend health error: backend socket missing: /run/noemaforge/llm/backends/main.sock
backend chat error: backend socket missing: /run/noemaforge/llm/backends/main.sock
```

## Expected behavior

For `runtime_only`, post-install smoke should validate what the profile promises:

```text
gateway health: ok
ToolProxy health: ok
main backend: skipped_expected_runtime_only
overall: pass or degraded, not fail
```

The existing backend-required smoke is still useful, but it should be explicitly tied to `bootstrap_cpu_llm`, `heavy_manual`, or `smoke-main` modes.

## Suggested fix

1. Add `noemaforge smoke --profile runtime_only` or `noemaforge smoke --gateway-only`.
2. Make `noemaforge smoke` infer the active/specified profile when possible.
3. In `runtime_only`, treat missing main backend socket as expected.
4. Keep backend health/chat checks mandatory only for profiles where a backend is expected.
5. Update first-run/re-entry docs so post-install validation uses the correct smoke command for the selected profile.

## Why this matters

The current smoke output makes a successful safe-core install/start look failed. It can misdirect debugging toward backend/LLM problems even when the selected install/start profile intentionally avoids launching a model.
title: Post-install smoke should be profile-aware: runtime_only should not fail on intentionally missing main backend
